D_vikings_cover_standard.text: COVER PRODUCTION STANDARD: Finished full-color portrait comic-book cover in the established Vikings 2026 illustrated language: clearly drawn and painted, controlled texture, expressive faces, believable anatomy, and tactile New York environments. The image must remain unmistakably illustration rather than photography or prestige-TV key art. Avoid photographic skin, lens effects, over-rendered fur, excessive bokeh, and cinematic orange/blue grading. Keep a strong one-second read and one dominant issue-specific image. Each issue's recipe defines a different graphic architecture; do not fall back to the same posed ensemble, foreground-observer, or cinematic tableau solution. Preserve human dignity and grounded documentary comedy.

D_vikings_cover_trade_dress.text: COVER TRADE-DRESS REFERENCE GATE: Before generating any Vikings 2026 cover, retrieve and visually pixel-read production/references/vikings-2026/assets/covers/issue-01-cover-trade-dress.jpg. Use only its established publication architecture as authority: the large white municipal-publication field, boxed STAR SPLITTER / VISIONS publisher mark, year-and-issue number, enormous condensed VIKINGS 2026! wordmark, thin horizontal rules, narrow all-caps issue subtitle, spacing rhythm, and transition into the illustration. Keep this top band deliberately dry, bureaucratic, and essentially fixed across the run. Do not reinterpret it as fantasy branding, parchment, runes, decorative shields, heroic typography, or faux-medieval ornament. Apart from required trade dress, readable environmental text should generally disappear unless the exact cover concept truly requires it; never invent signs, ads, labels, blurbs, or promotional copy.

D_vikings_cover_new_york_indifference.text: NEW YORK BACKGROUND BEHAVIOR: Use ordinary New Yorkers only when they serve the specific composition. Routine indifference is a social condition, not a requirement to place foreground commuters around the Vikings. Background people may continue working, waiting, walking, reading, boarding, serving, or filling out forms without spectacle, but keep them sparse when the image benefits from solitude or graphic clarity. Some covers should contain almost no visible background people. Do not use foreground heads, reaction crowds, gawking, pointing, photographing, or 'look at the Vikings' staging as a default solution.

D_vikings_cover_character_identity.text: CANONICAL CHARACTER IDENTITY: Actual established visual references are absolute. Resolve and pixel-read the strongest released or explicitly approved reference for every recurring character before generation; do not reconstruct faces from prose when pixels exist. Bjorn and Gunnar must never substitute for one another: Bjorn is the close-cropped, short-bearded, serious leader; Gunnar is the long-haired navigator with an enormous beard and black eye paint. Astrid and both male Kin retain their exact individual faces, bodies, hair, clothing, relative scale, and distinguishing features. Never average the household into interchangeable fantasy Vikings.
